did_you_know.text: The title attributes the psalm to David and connects it with the time when the Philistines seized him in Gath.
The psalm opens with a plea for mercy—“Be gracious to me, O God”—and describes continual pressure from enemies throughout the day.
The psalmist presents a process of confronting fear: even when a day of fear comes, he chooses to trust in God.
This verse brings together three central themes of the psalm: praise for God’s word, trust in God, and freedom from fear of people.
The enemies do more than threaten him with force; they also occupy themselves with the psalmist’s words and plot evil against him.
The image of tears being collected in a wineskin expresses the psalmist’s request that God remember his suffering and wanderings.
The psalmist repeats the theme of praising God’s word and refers to God in two forms of the divine name: “in God” and “in the LORD.”
The confidence expressed earlier returns here in similar wording: the psalmist is not afraid and asks what human beings can do to him.
After describing his deliverance, the psalmist remembers his vows and commits to fulfilling them through thanksgiving to God.
The conclusion of the psalm presents deliverance as a passage from death to life: God saves the soul, keeps the feet from stumbling, and enables the psalmist to walk before him in the light of life.
